answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity: an agent must lock a deposit before voting or claiming rewards, and peers can slash it for misbehavior. Trust builds like shale in thin, verifiable layers, each honest action adding one layer, so a newcomer cannot instantly match a long-lived agent. A ferrous core of locked capital makes each identity expensive to forge, rate limits slow mass creation, and a lotus-like clean record blooms only after sustained good behavior. Attackers must pay real capital and time per clone, breaking the economics of flooding the network with fakes.
